themes_detail.label: Dead Trees Proliferating
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints spiked to 9 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.9 weekly complaints—a 380% increase (z-score: 4.91)—suggesting rapid environmental degradation or delayed maintenance across the district that warrants urgent investigation.
evidence: 9 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Long-standing CB budget request for street lights and infrastructure suggests broader maintenance gaps in district
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Dept on whether budget constraints or staffing shortages are delaying tree maintenance in St. George/Stapleton
Map the geographic distribution of complaints to identify whether one neighborhood or waterfront area is disproportionately affected

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints (residential and other) jumped to 28 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 12.4 weekly—a 126% spike (z-score: 4.11)—indicating a sudden disruption to neighborhood quality of life that may correlate with construction, events, or new commercial activity.
evidence: 28 noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 12.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Noise-Residential is also a top-10 complaint category overall (1,209 complaints in 90 days), suggesting chronic baseline issue now worsening
reporting_angles: Cross-reference this week's spike with DOB permit filings (628 recent alterations/new buildings) to determine if construction is the driver
Interview residents in highest-complaint areas about source: nightlife, construction, traffic, or other; identify which blocks are most affected

themes_detail.label: Lot Condition Crisis Emerges
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.2 weekly—a 1100% spike (z-score: 6.35)—suggesting sudden deterioration of vacant or underutilized properties that may pose blight or safety risks.
evidence: 3 lot condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
1100% spike with z-score of 6.35 (highest statistical anomaly this week)
CB budget request for addressing illegal conversions and building uses (Department of Buildings) suggests underlying property-use chaos
reporting_angles: Obtain specific addresses of the 3 complaints and conduct site visits to document visible blight; cross-check against DOB records
Interview Department of Buildings about enforcement capacity and whether illegal conversions are tied to property abandonment

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (likely Uber/Lyft-related) jumped to 7 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 1.5 weekly—a 367% increase (z-score: 4.92)—suggesting congestion, illegal parking, or safety concerns tied to ride-sharing expansion in the district.
evidence: 7 for-hire vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Illegal Parking (1,736 complaints in 90 days) is second-highest complaint category; ride-sharing may be exacerbating
reporting_angles: Interview TLC about complaint patterns and enforcement in CD 501; determine if ride-sharing pickup zones are inadequate
Survey residents and local business owners about how for-hire vehicles are affecting street safety and parking availability

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Spike (3 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked to 4 THREE WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 0.1 weekly—a 3100% increase (z-score: 11.72, highest z-score in dataset)—suggesting either new enforcement action or a surge in illegal street vending that requires investigation.
evidence: 4 vendor enforcement complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
3100% spike with z-score of 11.72 (highest statistical anomaly in dataset, though older)
No recent Reddit or news coverage of vendor issues; signal may have already resolved or been under-reported
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD and Department of Consumer Affairs to learn what triggered the enforcement action and whether it is ongoing
Interview street vendors about whether they were targeted; assess whether enforcement has been sustained or was a one-time sweep
